base_source: TTM through Q2 2026 from EDGAR 10-Q YTD (OCF $2,325M = FY25 $2,197M - H1'25 $1,049M + H1'26 $1,177M; capex $411M; SBC $116M; OE $1,798M / 1,922M diluted shares = $0.9355). Engine normalized median-of-3-FY base was $0.824.
method_range_note: Preliminary run (normalized $0.82 base, engine growth -4.9% incl. spin-artifact dilution adj.) gave weighted IRR 6.1% / IV@15% $5.39; final TTM-base run gives 7.7% / $7.36. All defensible variants are Tier D; even super bull alone is 10.9%. Engine net debt ($391M) misses discontinued LongTermDebt tag — actual net debt ~$7.37B (4.1x TTM OE) at 2026-06-28, resolved manually in analysis.md.
moat_justification: Category-leading brands (Tylenol, Listerine, Band-Aid, Neutrogena, Aveeno, Zyrtec), ~60% gross margin and price-led organic growth prove pricing power, plus global pharmacy/shelf distribution scale — against five years of ~0% revenue growth, private-label and retailer pressure, no patent exclusivity, post-spin Skin Health share loss, tariff/input-cost squeeze, and the revived Tylenol litigation overhang.
name: Kenvue Inc.
one_liner: Iconic-brand consumer-health portfolio, moat 6/10, with real TTM owner's earnings of $0.94/share — but standalone it clears 15% only at ~$7.36 (margin of safety ~$5.50-6.00); at $17.76 the price is the Kimberly-Clark deal consideration (~$17.87 at KMB $98.29), so the 7.7% weighted IRR is the break-value downside if the Q4 2026 close fails.
